sheet-1-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1 shows the centre of the village of Pedricktown in Oldmans Township, Salem County, at 50 feet to an inch. Auburn Road runs across the top of the part, with only its south side drawn; the north side belongs to sheet 2. At the upper left Auburn Road meets East Mill Road, West Mill Road and the end of Railroad Avenue (lettered R.R. Av.) at the village crossroads. West Mill Road runs down the left edge towards the south-west, and Cherry leaves it to the east, turns north and rejoins Auburn Road, so that the part shows one complete block and the lots south of Cherry. The block is lined with frame dwellings, numbered 1 to 29 along Auburn Road, with sheds, garages and coops behind. Near the crossroads stand a brick bank and a small building holding the fire department and borough hall, with a few store and dwelling buildings along West Mill Road. South of Cherry are further dwellings and outbuildings, including a concrete-block garage. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the streets with dwelling hydrants. Block numbers 2, 3, 7 and 13 are printed in the blocks. The scale bar is drawn at the lower left, and a compass rose at the lower right shows north towards the upper left. The upper half of the sheet, with the key map, title cartouche, index and the depot area, is not part of this part.
notes: Auburn Road is today South Railroad Avenue.
East Mill Road and West Mill Road are today East Mill Street and West Mill Street.
R.R. Av. at the crossroads is Railroad Avenue, today North Railroad Avenue.
Cherry is today Cherry Street.
Bank, fire department and borough hall at the crossroads.

Map, 50 ft. Part 1 (lower): Auburn Rd (S Railroad Ave), W Mill Rd, Cherry around the village centre. Part 2 (upper left): West Jersey & Seashore R.R. depot area on Railroad Av about 1 mile NW (Geo. R. Pedrick & Son seed warehouses). Key map (800 ft to an inch), title, index and legend at upper right are not mapped.

sheet-1-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 1 is the railroad depot of Pedricktown on the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, about a mile north-west of the village centre on Railroad Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing to the upper left. The single main track (lettered W.J.&S.R.R.) runs straight up the part and is crossed near the bottom by Railroad Avenue, which runs from the upper left towards the lower right. Beside the main track stand the passenger depot with a platform and a freight house, a water closet and a small coal building, and to the west a curving siding serves a second freight house. Further west a second siding runs past an ice house and a long produce storage building. East of the track a coal pile is marked and the large property of Geo. R. Pedrick and Son, wholesale seed growers, has an L-shaped produce warehouse and a small office. A dwelling hydrant and a 4-inch water pipe are drawn along Railroad Avenue, and two small buildings stand on its south side. Block numbers 1, 4, 5 and 6 are printed. The part is bounded by a heavy line on its right side, which separates it from the key map of the town, and by the heavy line across the middle of the sheet.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today North Railroad Avenue.
The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad is today Conrail's Penns Grove Secondary.
The part is placed from the crossing of Railroad Avenue and the railroad alone (one point, scale from the sheet, rotation from the measured lines).

Map, 50 ft. Part 1 (lower): Auburn Rd (S Railroad Ave), W Mill Rd, Cherry around the village centre. Part 2 (upper left): West Jersey & Seashore R.R. depot area on Railroad Av about 1 mile NW (Geo. sheet-2-1.description: Sheet 2, main part, shows East Mill Road running north from the village crossroads at Auburn Road and Railroad Avenue to Oldmans Creek, at 50 feet to an inch, with north towards the upper left. Along the bottom of the part Auburn Road is drawn from the crossroads east to Cherry Street, with its north side in full: a printing shop, a general store, store houses, a lumber storage shed and dwellings near the crossroads, the brick public school (heated by steam, lit by electricity), further dwellings, a vacant blacksmith shop and part of the cemetery at the lower right. On the west side of the crossroads, along Railroad Avenue, stand a public garage with auto repair shop and several dwellings. East Mill Road is lined on both sides with frame dwellings and outbuildings, numbered 2 to 48, with large deep lots on the west side. At its north end, on the bank of Oldmans Creek, lie the flour mill premises of H. S. Justice and Co., with a mill, cement and flour warehouses, a long lumber shed and basket storage. The heavy line on the right separates the part from a section of West Mill Road (part 2). Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches and dwelling hydrants are drawn in the streets, and the scale bar is at the bottom.
notes: Auburn Road is today South Railroad Avenue.
Railroad Avenue is today North Railroad Avenue.
East Mill Road and West Mill Road are today East Mill Street and West Mill Street.
H. S. Justice and Co. flour mill on Oldmans Creek.
Public school on Auburn Road.
Rotation set from the line of East Mill Road (a hand-made point on the modern street centreline), since the two junctions on Auburn Road lie along one line.

Map, 50 ft. Part 1: E Mill Rd from Auburn Rd/Railroad Av north to Oldmans Creek (H. S. Justice & Co. flour mill) and the Auburn Rd frontage east to Cherry St. Part 2 (upper right, behind heavy line): W Mill Rd south of Cherry; continues on sheet 4 part 2 (A-B match line).

sheet-2-2.description: The upper right part of sheet 2, set off by a heavy line, shows West Mill Road south of Cherry Street, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Cherry Street enters at the top right and meets West Mill Road, which runs down the part towards the south-west. Both sides of the road are lined with frame dwellings, numbered 9 to 28 and then 149 to 199, with stables, sheds and small outbuildings behind them. On the west side stands a concrete-block public garage with electric light and hot water heating. Towards the bottom the lots become larger and mostly empty. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B crosses the road near the bottom, marking where the drawing continues on sheet 4. An 8-inch water pipe runs along West Mill Road and a 4-inch pipe along Cherry Street, with dwelling hydrants. Block numbers 4 and 7 are printed, and street widths of 45 to 55 feet are written across the road.
notes: East Mill Road and West Mill Road are today East Mill Street and West Mill Street.
Placed from the Cherry Street junction and a hand-made point on the modern West Mill Street centreline at the A-B match line (812 ft along the road at the sheet scale); low confidence along the road.
Continues on sheet 4, part 2, at the A-B match line.

Map, 50 ft. Part 1: E Mill Rd from Auburn Rd/Railroad Av north to Oldmans Creek (H. S. Justice & Co. flour mill) and the Auburn Rd frontage east to Cherry St. Part 2 (upper right, behind heavy line): W Mill Rd south of Cherry; continues on sheet 4 part 2 (A-B match line).

sheet-3-1.description: The top strip of sheet 3 shows Railroad Avenue running west from West Mill Road, East Mill Road and Cherry Street at the village crossroads, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Both sides of Railroad Avenue are drawn, with lots numbered 2 to 36 on alternate sides. Near the crossroads stand a hall with stores and the post office, a bakery with an office, a restaurant, a sausage factory, offices and dwellings; further west are the Hudson M. E. Church, auto repair shops, a wagon shed, a blacksmith and wheelwright shop and a row of frame dwellings with stables and garages behind them. A 6-inch water pipe with dwelling hydrants runs along Railroad Avenue and an 8-inch pipe along West Mill Road. Block numbers 1, 2 and 4 are printed. Arrows at the left edge show that the street continues on the strip below on the same sheet.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today North Railroad Avenue.
East Mill Road and West Mill Road are today East Mill Street and West Mill Street.
Hudson M. E. Church and the post office on Railroad Avenue.
Placed from the crossroads, the Cherry Street junction and a hand-made point on the modern street centreline at the left end.

Map, 50 ft. Four strips of Railroad Av (N Railroad Ave) running NW from the village centre: part 1 (top) from W Mill/E Mill Rd west; part 2 (middle); part 3 (lower); part 4 (lower-left inset). Only part 1 has street junctions; parts 2 to 4 are frontage strips along one road. Parts 2 to 4 are placed by continuity along the modern road (no junctions); the chain ends within about 5 m of the depot part of sheet 1.

sheet-3-2.description: The middle strip of sheet 3 continues Railroad Avenue north-west of the top strip, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The road runs across the strip from left to right, with a 4-inch water pipe and a few dwelling hydrants in it. The frontage is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with stables, garages, coops and small sheds behind them, and wide stretches of open land between. House numbers are arbitrary, with lots numbered 541 to 562 on the north side and 625 to 652 on the south side. The strip contains no cross street, so nothing but the line of the road ties it to the modern map. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B at the left edge marks the continuation on the lower strip. This stretch of Railroad Avenue led from the village to the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad depot about a mile out of town.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today North Railroad Avenue.

No street junction: placed by continuity with the adjoining strips, on two hand-made points on the modern street centreline at the sheet scale (7.8 px/ft); low confidence along the road. The chain ends within about 5 m of where the depot part of sheet 1 begins, which supports it.

sheet-3-3.description: The lower strip of sheet 3 continues Railroad Avenue further north-west, where the road begins to bend towards the north, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The road runs across the strip from left to right, with a 4-inch water pipe and a few dwelling hydrants in it. The frontage is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with stables, garages, coops and small sheds behind them, and wide stretches of open land between. House numbers are arbitrary, with lots numbered 525 to 536 and 589 to 597 and 617 to 618. The strip contains no cross street, so nothing but the line of the road ties it to the modern map. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B at the right edge joins it to the middle strip; at the left the road continues in the small strip at the lower left. This stretch of Railroad Avenue led from the village to the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad depot about a mile out of town.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today North Railroad Avenue.

No street junction: placed by continuity with the adjoining strips, on two hand-made points on the modern street centreline at the sheet scale (7.8 px/ft); low confidence along the road. The chain ends within about 5 m of where the depot part of sheet 1 begins, which supports it.

sheet-3-4.description: The small strip at the lower left of sheet 3, set off by a heavy line, shows the farthest stretch of Railroad Avenue drawn on this sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. The road runs across the strip from left to right, with a 4-inch water pipe and a few dwelling hydrants in it. The frontage is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with stables, garages, coops and small sheds behind them, and wide stretches of open land between. House numbers are arbitrary, with lots numbered 587 and 588. The strip contains no cross street, so nothing but the line of the road ties it to the modern map. Arrows at its right edge show that it continues from the lower strip of the same sheet; beyond its left edge the road leads on to the railroad depot on sheet 1. This stretch of Railroad Avenue led from the village to the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad depot about a mile out of town.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today North Railroad Avenue.

No street junction: placed by continuity with the adjoining strips, on two hand-made points on the modern street centreline at the sheet scale (7.8 px/ft); low confidence along the road. The chain ends within about 5 m of where the depot part of sheet 1 begins, which supports it.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4 shows West Mill Road running south-west from the village to the five-way junction with Porcupine Road, Pennsgrove Road, Perkintown Road and Straugns Mill Road, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Along the east side of West Mill Road are frame dwellings numbered 175 to 179 with stores and stables, then the First Baptist Church (with an addition being built) and its wagon shed, and a large cemetery reaching back to Straugns Mill Road. The west side has a few dwellings on deep lots. At the junction stand dwellings on Porcupine Road, two auto repairing shops, one of concrete block, on Straugns Mill Road beside a pond, and dwellings along Pennsgrove Road and Perkintown Road. An 8-inch water pipe runs down West Mill Road and on along Perkintown Road towards the Penns Grove water works. Block numbers 4, 7, 10, 11 and 12 are printed, and road widths of 25 to 43 feet are written at the junction. The heavy line at the upper left separates a further section of West Mill Road (part 2).
notes: East Mill Road and West Mill Road are today East Mill Street and West Mill Street.

Pennsgrove Road is today Pennsgrove-Pedricktown Road; Straugns Mill Road is today Straughens Mill Road; Perkintown Road is probably today's Pennsville-Pedricktown Road, which now meets Pennsgrove-Pedricktown Road about 100 m west of the junction.
The junction has been realigned since: placed from one hand-picked point at the old junction, scale from the sheet and rotation from West Mill Road; low confidence.
First Baptist Church and cemetery.

Map, 50 ft. Part 1 (main): W Mill Rd south to the five-way junction with Porcupine Rd, Pennsgrove Rd, Perkintown Rd and Straugns Mill Rd; First Baptist Church and cemetery. Part 2 (upper left, behind heavy line): W Mill Rd with Geo. R. Pedrick & Son seed warehouses, continuing from sheet 2 part 2 (A-B match line). Part 2 is placed by the A-B line carried from sheet 2 part 2; its lower end reaches about 80 m past where part 1 begins on the ground (part 1 is anchored on the realigned five-way junction), so one of them is off along West Mill Road; both low confidence.

sheet-4-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 4, set off by a heavy line, shows a further section of West Mill Road between the part on sheet 2 and the main part of sheet 4, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B at the top joins it to sheet 2. The east side of the road is taken up largely by the premises of Geo. R. Pedrick and Son, wholesale seed growers, with a seed warehouse, a long green house, corn cribs, a water tank, sheds and a large barn, followed by frame dwellings numbered about 181 to 187 on deep lots. The west side has a few dwellings and outbuildings. An 8-inch water pipe with dwelling hydrants runs along the road. Block numbers 4 and 7 are printed.
notes: East Mill Road and West Mill Road are today East Mill Street and West Mill Street.
Geo. R. Pedrick and Son, wholesale seed growers.

No street junction: placed from the A-B match line carried from sheet 2 part 2, with the sheet scale and the direction of West Mill Road; low confidence. The chain from sheet 2 reaches about 80 m further south than where the main part of sheet 4 begins, so one of the two is misplaced along the road or the sheets are not drawn to a uniform scale.
